strengths: Novel and well-supported empirical observation that attention sparsity naturally reveals a tri-modal distribution corresponding to reasoning/execution/transition 'thought types' in LRM chains-of-thought, providing a principled (non-keyword-based) basis for CoT decomposition.

Strong algorithm-system co-design: the paper doesn't just propose a compression heuristic but also identifies and solves a real systems bottleneck (gather-based compaction overhead) via the Continuous Thinking (CT) kernel extension to PagedAttention, backed by concrete profiling (up to 37x TPOT slowdown for naive gather).

Extensive and diverse experimental validation across many model families (DeepSeek-R1-Distill 8B/70B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B, GPT-OSS 20B/120B, QwQ-32B, AceReason-14B, MobileLLM-R1-950M) and benchmarks (AIME, LiveCodeBench, MATH-500, GSM8K), which strengthens generality claims.

Thorough ablation studies covering refresh rate, number of thought types, optimal calibration layers, minimum token retention, block size, and data format choices, which help justify design decisions rather than treating them as arbitrary hyperparameters.

Reports both accuracy and systems-level throughput/latency gains with reasonable baselines (H2O, RaaS, R-KV, LazyEviction, KIVI, PM-KVQ), and includes iso-batch/iso-compression comparisons to isolate the specific contribution of the CT kernel versus the compression algorithm itself.

Includes generalization experiments beyond LRMs (LongWriter with standard LLMs) and an interesting qualitative failure-mode analysis (endless-loop behavior when transition thoughts are fully evicted), adding some interpretability to the method's design choices.
weaknesses: The core thought-decomposition mechanism relies on layer-specific sparsity thresholds calibrated via KDE on a small offline set (100 prompts from s1K); the paper acknowledges some layers/models (e.g., certain GPT-OSS-20B layers) show ambiguous tri-modal boundaries, raising concerns about robustness and transferability of thresholds across domains, prompt distributions, or future model architectures not covered in calibration.

The counterfactual thought-importance analysis (Fig. 4, establishing R>E>T) and the pairwise thought-association analysis (Fig. 6, establishing TBE's design) are demonstrated primarily on GPT-OSS-20B with only a couple of example prompts; it is unclear how robustly this hierarchy generalizes across models and problem types, especially given the paper's own admission of high-importance 'outlier' transition thoughts that can break the general ordering.

The system implementation is only a 'proof-of-concept' built on Hugging Face Transformers with a custom Triton PagedAttention variant, not integrated into production serving frameworks (vLLM, TRT-LLM) as explicitly noted in Limitations; this weakens the practical significance of the throughput claims, since real-world serving stacks have additional complexities (continuous batching, scheduling) not evaluated here.

The method involves a fairly large number of interacting hyperparameters (refresh period τ, group size g, retention schedule R, number of thoughts |T|, optimal layer subset L*, quantization bit assignment), most tuned via ablation on specific model/dataset pairs; the reproducibility and sensitivity of the full pipeline to these joint choices on unseen settings is not deeply analyzed.

Some abstract/intro claims (e.g., 'near-lossless accuracy with <5% of the original KV cache') are optimistic averages; Figure 8 shows accuracy drops of several percentage points to >10% in some low-budget regimes (e.g., token budget=64), and the 'near-lossless' framing could be more carefully qualified relative to the compression level achieved.

The interaction between quantization-induced generation-length inflation and the hybrid scheme's effectiveness (Section 2, Table 3) is an important but somewhat underexplored phenomenon; the paper offers an intuitive explanation ('hybrid regularizes inflation') but no rigorous mechanistic analysis or theoretical grounding for why combining eviction with quantization curbs this inflation.

strengths: Strong, well-designed motivating analysis: the paper empirically identifies a tri-modal attention sparsity pattern corresponding to reasoning/execution/transition 'thought types' and backs this up with counterfactual importance (KL-divergence rollouts) and pairwise thought-association studies, giving the method a solid empirical grounding rather than being purely heuristic.

The hybrid quantization+eviction design is well motivated by a clear analysis (Fig. 2) showing why pure quantization inflates generation length while pure eviction plateaus in accuracy — this justifies the core architectural choice non-trivially.

Comprehensive systems contribution: identification and quantification of gather-based compaction overhead (up to 37x TPOT slowdown) and a genuinely useful fix (Continuous Thinking kernel extending PagedAttention with soft eviction masks and thought-aware paging) that avoids compaction while preserving the standard attention kernel.

Very extensive empirical evaluation across many model families (DeepSeek-R1-Distill 8B/70B, GPT-OSS 20B/120B, AceReason-14B, QwQ-32B, MobileLLM-R1-950M, Qwen3) and benchmarks (AIME, LiveCodeBench, MATH-500, GSM8K, LongWriter, LongBench v2), with consistent near-lossless accuracy at <5% KV cache budget.

Strong efficiency results with credible throughput/latency measurements (up to 5.8x throughput over R-KV, 15.8x over FullKV at accuracy-preserving budgets) validated on both A100 and GH200, plus a vLLM integration experiment corroborating gains beyond the custom HF Transformers stack.

Thorough ablations isolating the contribution of each component (TBQ vs TBE vs combined), sensitivity to refresh rate, number of thought types, calibration layers, minimum retention, block size, and quantization data formats, which strengthens the causal story behind design choices.

Reasonable theoretical support (KV permutation invariance proof) explaining why the CT kernel can avoid token reordering, and generalization experiments to non-reasoning LLMs (LongWriter) show the framework is not narrowly limited to LRMs.
weaknesses: The thought decomposition relies on offline KDE-based threshold calibration per model/layer subset, which the paper itself acknowledges can be ambiguous or fail to produce clean tri-modal structure in some layers/models (e.g., GPT-OSS 'hard to distinguish cases' in Fig. 14); this raises concerns about robustness and the amount of per-model tuning required for practitioners to reproduce results.

The method has many interacting hyperparameters (refresh interval τ, group size g, retention schedule R, number of thought types, calibration layer subset L*, K-means eviction, per-format scale factors for ternary/NVFP4/FP8), which raises reproducibility concerns and makes it unclear how sensitive real-world deployment would be to calibration-set choice (calibrated only on 100 s1K prompts).

The categorization function ϕ is only an approximate, correlational proxy for semantic thought types (attention sparsity thresholds), and while the counterfactual analyses support importance ranking, the causal validity of assigning discrete category labels via simple sparsity thresholds under all reasoning styles/domains is not rigorously established beyond a few benchmarks.

Some illustrative evidence (e.g., the appendix reasoning trace where GPT-OSS fails/loops when a transition thought is over-compressed) is somewhat anecdotal and mixes model-intrinsic weaknesses with the compression algorithm's behavior; it is not clear this ablation isolates ThinKV-specific failure modes versus general eviction risks that would occur under any overly aggressive compression of trajectory-changing content.

Baseline comparison fairness is not fully detailed — it is unclear whether all eviction/quantization baselines (H2O, RaaS, R-KV, LazyEviction, KIVI, PM-KVQ) were equally hyperparameter-tuned for their respective methods, especially at very low token budgets where the reported accuracy gaps are large.

Treating all prefill tokens uniformly as 'R type' is a simplifying design decision without deep justification or ablation, despite prefill potentially containing execution/transition-like content in some domains (e.g., code repository context in the LongBench v2 experiment).

The paper is dense with heavy notation and many components described somewhat tersely in the main text (details deferred to a very long appendix), which could hinder clarity and independent reproducibility without the appendix and released code (no code release is explicitly mentioned).

strengths: Extensive empirical evaluation across many LRM families (DeepSeek-R1-Distill 8B/70B, GPT-OSS 20B/120B, AceReason-14B, QwQ-32B, MobileLLM-R1, Qwen3), datasets (AIME, LiveCodeBench, MATH-500, GSM8K), and an unusually thorough appendix with many ablations (refresh rate, block size, number of thought types, minimum retention, data format choice, generalization to LLMs, SnapKV integration, etc.).

The motivating analysis connecting attention sparsity patterns to a tri-modal decomposition of CoT, combined with counterfactual importance and pairwise association studies, provides a plausible mechanistic story for why token-level heuristics used by prior eviction methods (H2O, R-KV, RaaS, LazyEviction) underperform.

The system-level contribution (Continuous Thinking kernel extending PagedAttention with thought-aware, in-place slot reuse) directly targets a well-documented, quantitatively demonstrated bottleneck (gather-based compaction overhead), and the throughput/latency gains are large and consistently reproduced across A100/GH200 and both a custom HF-Transformers stack and a vLLM integration.

Reasonably comprehensive baseline coverage spanning both eviction (H2O, RaaS, R-KV, LazyEviction) and quantization (KIVI, PM-KVQ) families, plus iso-batch and iso-compression comparisons that help isolate the source of throughput gains (compression ratio vs. kernel design).
weaknesses: The central mechanism—online thought classification ϕ via attention-sparsity KDE thresholds—is never directly validated against any ground-truth labeling of thought type; the paper only shows illustrative keyword-based post-hoc interpretation of sparsity regions, but there is no confusion matrix, human-labeled agreement, or sensitivity analysis of classification accuracy, despite the entire compression scheme (TBQ/TBE) being built on top of this classifier.

There is a validity gap between how thought importance/association are established (expensive offline counterfactual KL-divergence rollouts over 50 samples, per Bogdan et al.) and how the online system actually operates (cheap attention-sparsity thresholds); the paper does not show these two signals are well correlated, so it's unclear the deployed heuristic actually tracks the causally-validated importance ordering (R>E>T).

Fixing |T|=3 despite acknowledging in §3.1 that 'some layers exhibit more than three sparsity regimes or ambiguous boundaries' (and GPT-OSS-20B examples of 'hard to distinguish cases' in the appendix) suggests the tri-modal decomposition may not generalize cleanly across architectures, and the paper doesn't quantify how often calibration fails or how brittle the chosen L* layer subset is across prompts/domains.

The method has many interacting hyperparameters (refresh period τ=128, group size g=16, retention schedule R={64,32,16,8,4}, precision assignment R4E4T2, block size, K-means eviction) that appear tuned on the s1K calibration set and held fixed; given the number of degrees of freedom, there is real risk of overfitting to the specific benchmarks/models tested, and no held-out generalization test to unseen task types (outside the LongWriter/LLM sanity check) is provided.

Accuracy evaluation uses pass@1 averaged over only 8 rollouts on relatively small benchmarks (e.g., 30-prompt AIME set), with no confidence intervals or variance reported, making it hard to assess whether reported <1-4% accuracy gaps versus FullKV are statistically meaningful or within noise.

The 'Think Before You Evict' endless-loop anecdote (Appendix E.17) and the qualitative reasoning-trace example are used as illustrative motivation but are single anecdotal cases rather than systematic failure-mode analysis.

Primary throughput/TPOT results are obtained on a self-modified Hugging Face Transformers + custom Triton PagedAttention stack that the authors themselves describe as 'not the most optimized'; while a vLLM integration is provided in the appendix, it is comparatively limited in scope (fewer batch sizes/configurations) and reads as a secondary validation rather than the primary evaluation vehicle, raising some concern about how representative the headline throughput numbers are of production serving systems.

The quantization baselines (KIVI, PM-KVQ) are relatively dated/simple compared to more recent quantization-eviction hybrids (e.g., MiniKV, Q-Hitter) that are only discussed in related work but not empirically compared against, weakening the claim of state-of-the-art status.

strengths: Well-motivated core insight: the paper empirically demonstrates via attention sparsity, counterfactual KL-divergence importance analysis, and pairwise thought-association studies that CoT can be decomposed into reasoning/execution/transition segments with distinct importance and redundancy profiles, providing a principled basis for the compression algorithm rather than an ad hoc heuristic.

Clear systems contribution: the 'Continuous Thinking' kernel extending PagedAttention to reuse evicted memory slots without gather-based compaction is well justified by a careful profiling study (Section 5.1) showing up to 37x TPOT slowdown from gather operations, and the proof of the permutation invariance of attention (Theorem 1) rigorously justifies why reordering can be avoided.

Extensive and diverse empirical evaluation: results span DeepSeek-R1-Distill (8B/70B), GPT-OSS (20B/120B), AceReason-14B, QwQ-32B, MobileLLM-R1-950M, and Qwen3-8B across AIME, LiveCodeBench, MATH-500, GSM8K, and LongWriter, with consistent near-lossless accuracy at <5% KV cache and substantial throughput/latency gains (up to 5.8x throughput, 58% lower latency in multi-user settings).

Thorough ablations isolating the contribution of each component (TBQ vs TBE vs combined), sensitivity to hyperparameters (refresh rate, number of layers, number of thought types, minimum retention, block size, data formats), and comparisons on both eviction-only and quantization-only baselines, giving good insight into why the method works (e.g., Top-10 attention recall rate analysis).

Validation in a real serving framework (vLLM) in the appendix strengthens practical relevance beyond the custom PagedAttention proof-of-concept used for the main experiments, and additional experiments (LLM generalization, GPT-OSS-120B, integration with SnapKV for prefill) demonstrate the framework's broader applicability.
weaknesses: The three-way thought decomposition (R/E/T) relies on sparsity-threshold calibration via KDE mode detection, which the authors themselves note is unreliable in some layers/models (e.g., 'hard to distinguish cases' for GPT-OSS in Appendix E.4); the robustness of this categorization procedure across arbitrary new models/architectures is not deeply analyzed beyond the specific models tested.

The counterfactual thought-importance analysis (Section 3.2), which underlies the R>E>T precision ordering used throughout the paper, is validated on a single model (GPT-OSS-20B) and only two benchmarks, leaving some uncertainty about whether this importance ordering generalizes as robustly as claimed to the other five+ models evaluated later.

Several key hyperparameters (retention schedule R={64,32,16,8,4}, refresh period τ=128, precision assignment R4E4T2, group size, K-means eviction) appear to be manually tuned based on empirical observation rather than derived from a principled optimization, and while ablations are provided, the sensitivity of results to joint interactions between these hyperparameters across different model families is not fully explored.

The system implementation is fairly complex (custom Triton kernels, modified block tables with multiple new metadata fields, K-means-based eviction, group quantization with multiple data formats), which may pose reproducibility challenges; code/kernel release is not explicitly confirmed in the manuscript.

The main throughput/latency results are obtained on a custom Hugging-Face-based PagedAttention implementation described as a 'proof of concept' rather than a fully optimized serving stack, and while vLLM validation is provided in the appendix, it is comparatively limited (fewer configurations) relative to the main-text results.
